content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 2

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 16

---

## Disagreement 001 — v. 1: "also found in the records"

- **EMET:** "It is also found in the records"
- **LOGOS:** "One finds also in the records"
- **PNEUMA:** "The same records also tell us"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's phrasing is more idiomatic and connects explicitly to the prior chapter. EMET is passive; LOGOS is impersonal-active. SOPHIA adopts LOGOS.

## Disagreement 002 — v. 2: "charged" vs. "instructed" vs. "urged"

- **EMET:** "charged those who were being deported"
- **LOGOS:** "instructed those who were being deported"
- **PNEUMA:** "urged the exiles"
- **Note:** Greek *eneteilen* — commanded/charged. EMET most closely follows the authoritative tone. PNEUMA's "urged" softens the imperative force. SOPHIA uses "charged."

## Disagreement 003 — v. 2: "led astray in their minds"

- **EMET:** "led astray in their minds"
- **LOGOS:** "led astray in their thoughts"
- **PNEUMA:** "seduced by their splendor"
- **Note:** PNEUMA interprets the mental seduction as aesthetic, adding "splendor." EMET and LOGOS are closer to the Greek *planēthēnai tais dianoiais*. SOPHIA uses "led astray in their thoughts."

## Disagreement 004 — v. 4: "tent and the ark"

- **EMET:** "the tent and the ark should follow with him"
- **LOGOS:** "the tent of meeting and the ark should accompany him"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Tent of Meeting and the ark of the covenant should be carried with him"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "of the covenant" to the ark description. The Greek simply has *tēn kibōton* — the ark. LOGOS adds "of meeting" to the tent, which is conventional. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 005 — v. 5: "cave-dwelling" vs. "cave"

- **EMET:** "found a cave-dwelling"
- **LOGOS:** "found a cave there"
- **PNEUMA:** "discovered a cave there"
- **Note:** Greek *spēlaion* — cave. EMET's "cave-dwelling" adds nuance not in the Greek. SOPHIA uses "found a cave there."

## Disagreement 006 — v. 7: Jeremiah's response

- **EMET:** "he rebuked them and declared"
- **LOGOS:** "he rebuked them and declared"
- **PNEUMA:** "he confronted them and said"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree. PNEUMA's "confronted" adds a confrontational edge. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

## Disagreement 007 — v. 8: Cloud and glory

- **EMET:** "the glory of the LORD and the cloud will appear"
- **LOGOS:** "the glory of the LORD will appear, together with the cloud"
- **PNEUMA:** "The glory of the LORD will appear — the cloud will be seen again"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's em-dash separates cloud and glory for dramatic effect. LOGOS subordinates the cloud to the glory. EMET coordinates them. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 008 — v. 9: "possessed of wisdom"

- **EMET:** "being possessed of wisdom"
- **LOGOS:** "possessing wisdom"
- **PNEUMA:** "in his wisdom"
- **Note:** EMET is archaic in register. LOGOS and PNEUMA both update naturally. SOPHIA uses "possessing wisdom."

## Disagreement 009 — v. 12: "kept the eight days"

- **EMET:** "Solomon also kept the eight days"
- **LOGOS:** "Solomon kept the eight days of dedication"
- **PNEUMA:** "Solomon likewise observed eight days of celebration"
- **Note:** LOGOS adds "of dedication" for clarity; PNEUMA uses "celebration." SOPHIA follows LOGOS for precision.

## Disagreement 010 — v. 13: "records and memoirs"

- **EMET:** "records and the memoirs of Nehemiah"
- **LOGOS:** "records and in the memoirs of Nehemiah"
- **PNEUMA:** "the memoirs of Nehemiah"
- **Note:** PNEUMA omits "records and the." Greek has *en tais anagraphais* and *en tois apomnēmoneumasin*. EMET and LOGOS retain both terms. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 011 — v. 13: "books" vs. "writings"

- **EMET:** "books about the kings and the prophets, and the books of David"
- **LOGOS:** "writings about the kings and the prophets, the writings of David"
- **PNEUMA:** "the writings about the kings and the prophets, the psalms of David"
- **Note:** PNEUMA specifies "psalms" for the "writings of David," adding interpretive specificity. LOGOS uses "writings" throughout for consistency. SOPHIA follows LOGOS but notes PNEUMA's "psalms" is a reasonable interpretation.

## Disagreement 012 — v. 14: Judas's collection

- **EMET:** "gathered together all the books that had been scattered"
- **LOGOS:** "collected all the writings that had been scattered"
- **PNEUMA:** "gathered up all the books that had been scattered and lost"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "and lost" for emphasis. EMET uses "books," LOGOS "writings." SOPHIA uses "writings" for consistency with v. 13.

## Disagreement 013 — v. 21: "barbarian hordes"

- **EMET:** "put to flight the barbarian hordes"
- **LOGOS:** "drove away the barbarian hordes"
- **PNEUMA:** "routed those barbarian hordes"
- **Note:** Greek *tas barbariktas plēthyas* — the barbarian multitudes. PNEUMA's "routed" is a more emphatic military term. All three are acceptable. SOPHIA uses "drove off."

## Disagreement 014 — v. 22: "clemency"

- **EMET:** "with all his clemency became gracious"
- **LOGOS:** "in his great clemency became gracious"
- **PNEUMA:** "in his great kindness had compassion"
- **Note:** Greek *epieikeia* — reasonableness, clemency, graciousness. PNEUMA substitutes "kindness/compassion," which is warmer but less precise. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 015 — v. 27: Dinner party metaphor

- **EMET:** "just as it is not easy for one who prepares a banquet"
- **LOGOS:** "just as it is no light matter for one who prepares a feast"
- **PNEUMA:** "Think of someone throwing a dinner party"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's idiomatic rendering is lively but loses the "seeking benefit of others" element from the Greek. SOPHIA follows LOGOS for completeness.

## Disagreement 016 — v. 29: Architectural metaphor

- **EMET:** "just as the architect of a new house"
- **LOGOS:** "as the master builder of a new house"
- **PNEUMA:** "An architect overseeing new construction"
- **Note:** Greek *oikodespotēs* — actually "master of the house" (EMET/LOGOS are closer). PNEUMA reframes as "overseeing construction," which shifts the metaphor. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
